items.label: 2A
items.claim: UK university sequencing-services frameworks are awarded overwhelmingly to low-cost outsourcers (Novogene, Genewiz, Macrogen), as research buyers shift work away from in-house Illumina cores.
items.detail: University of Edinburgh's EC0900 Lot 1 short-read framework (award published 14 Jul 2022, contract signed 21 Apr 2022, £1.0M) went to seven suppliers: Anthony Nolan HLA labs, Earlham Institute, GENEWIZ UK, Macrogen Europe, MicrobesNG, Novogene (UK) and CeGaT. Leicester LUV01297 (award notice 9 Jun 2025, £1.0M, 10 bids) has four winners, including Genewiz, Eurofins and Novogene (UK) and Randox. Novogene and Genewiz won both frameworks, which gives UK academic buyers a pre-approved low-cost outsourcing route. Edinburgh's 2022 rules also direct users to internal resources first, with the framework as the fallback on 'capacity or cost'.
items.source_name: Find a Tender OCDS API (Cabinet Office), University of Edinburgh EC0900; University of Leicester LUV01297
items.why_new: Names the winners and £ values of two UK academic sequencing frameworks. Known items only say Leicester's 2025 framework went to four outsourcers.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Quality outweighs price heavily in UK academic sequencing frameworks, which goes against the idea that research buyers run a price-only race.
items.detail: Edinburgh EC0900 weighted award criteria at Quality 90 / Price 10, and the lot sub-frameworks (Lot 12 and Lot 13) used the same split. Leicester LUV01297 weighted Quality 75 / Price 25, and LSTM AF116 (tender 19 Mar 2025) weighted Quality 70 / Price 30. The price weight rose from 10% (2021) to 25–30% (2025), so price matters more than it did, but it is still a minority factor. This weakens the claim that academic sequencing is bought mainly on price, although 7 of 8 Edinburgh bids were SMEs, so the supplier base is competitive.
items.source_name: Find a Tender OCDS API, Edinburgh EC0900, LSTM AF116, Leicester LUV01297
items.why_new: Gives the criteria weights for three frameworks and a trend in the price weight. The known item F471 only says quality is weighted well above price.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Edinburgh is re-tendering its whole sequencing and genotyping framework (EC1066) as a single lot with no stated value, which signals more open competition among outsourcers for research sequencing.
items.detail: Planning notice 053109-2025 was published 2 Sep 2025 for EC1066 'Sequencing & Genotyping Services'. It is one planned lot with no value and no award criteria, and the next notice is dated 30 Jan 2026. The predecessor EC0900 was a lotted family (Lot 1 short read, Lot 12 transgenic genotyping, Lot 13 DNA/RNA extraction, up to 10 participants per lot). Consolidating to one lot lets multi-platform outsourcers bid for everything, including Illumina short-read work. A Jan 2026 contract notice was not found, so scope and pricing remain unknown.
items.source_name: Find a Tender OCDS API, University of Edinburgh EC1066
items.why_new: Gives the structure of Edinburgh's replacement framework (one lot, planned Jan 2026), not previously known.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: The LSTM sequencing framework (AF116) is small and mostly outsourced NGS spend: £300K over up to three years, with £280K in Lot 1 and £20K for Sanger.
items.detail: The tender notice 010265-2025 (19 Mar 2025) estimated £300,000 including VAT for 1+1+1 years, which is about £100K/yr, split Lot 1 'Next Generation & Third Generation' £280K and Lot 2 'Sanger' £20K. Bids were due 22 Apr 2025 and the award decision was estimated 10 May 2025. No award notice or supplier names were found, and the OCDS record still shows only the tender stage. At £280K over three years, the NGS spend is about £93K/yr, which is immaterial to Illumina but fits a pattern of small institutions buying sequencing as a service.
items.source_name: Find a Tender OCDS API, LSTM AF116
items.why_new: Quantifies the AF116 lot split and value, and confirms that no award exists.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Per-framework spend is small (about £1.0M per framework), and the incumbent outsourcers are broad service labs, so these frameworks are not a visible price attack on Illumina.
items.detail: Edinburgh EC0900 Lot 1 and Leicester LUV01297 each carry a £1.0M ceiling. Over the typical 3–4 year term that is about £0.25–0.33M/yr per university. Nothing in these notices names a non-Illumina sequencer or a price per Gb, and the notices do not show whether winners are shifting work to Ultima or Element. Some winners, such as Novogene, CeGaT and Macrogen, run Illumina-based production, so outsourcing may mean the same consumables bought in bulk rather than a lost Illumina sale.
items.source_name: Find a Tender, Leicester LUV01297 award notice; Edinburgh EC0900
items.why_new: Sizes the frameworks and says plainly that the notices carry no platform or price evidence.

notes: The OCDS API works for known ocids, but the list endpoint returns 1M+ characters unfiltered and cannot be keyword-searched through WebFetch. LSTM AF116 has no award release, and Edinburgh EC1066 has no contract notice after the Sep 2025 planning notice. Leicester's tender documents (Delta eSourcing) and Randox's role were not opened. Platform and price schedules sit in tender documents that need a login. Very little further evidence is left in these notices.
